How a rate is calculated

For each rarity, divide the number of cards observed by the number of packs opened. The result is observed copies per pack, not the probability that a pack contains at least one card of that rarity.

What a sample must show

A usable sample names its source, set, region, booster type, opening dates, pack count, cards per pack and counts for every observed rarity. Rarity totals must match the recorded card variants.

How to read the result

Openings vary. A sample describes what was observed, not a guaranteed result for your next pack. Without pack-level hit records, aggregated card counts cannot establish the chance of at least one hit.

Pokémon TCG booster expected value

Learn how observed openings and matching EUR prices can estimate a booster’s gross card value.

Data status

No validated opening sample with complete matching EUR Cardmarket prices is published yet. Numeric expected value is unavailable.

How value is estimated

Multiply each observed card-variant count by its matching Cardmarket EUR price. Add those amounts and divide by packs opened. Compare that gross card value with a matching booster price.

What prices must cover

The opening sample and price snapshot must match the set, region and booster type. Every observed card variant needs a corresponding Cardmarket EUR quote, and the booster price needs its own source.

An estimate, not a return

Market prices move. Condition, selling fees, shipping, taxes and unsold cards can change the amount received. An average from past openings does not promise a profitable pack.
